en:
The community orchard occupies a narrow strip of land between the railway and a public footpath. Volunteers keep a notebook beside the tool shed so that each team can see what was done the previous weekend. The notebook records watering, pruning and the replacement of wooden supports. A map on the first page identifies the varieties of apple and pear trees planted in each row.

During the spring open day, visitors compare flowers on the different trees. The guide explains how gardeners observe the first buds and record the dates when the petals open. Children make drawings of branches and collect the drawings in a folder for the local school. Several older residents bring photographs showing how the site looked before the orchard was established.

A small market takes place beside the entrance once a month. One stall sells handmade baskets, while another displays ceramic cups and plates. The organisers measure the available space and leave a wide path between the tables. A musician plays acoustic guitar near the far gate, where visitors can sit on benches and watch trains passing beyond the fence.

At the planning meeting, the team discusses the layout of the noticeboard and the position of a new rain gauge. The secretary prepares a simple timetable for the summer months. Every task has a named volunteer and an approximate completion date. The final agenda item concerns a collection of old maps that will be displayed during the autumn harvest event.

The pottery studio is preparing an exhibition of everyday vessels. Shelves along the wall hold bowls, cups and small pitchers made by students during the previous term. Each object is photographed beside a ruler before being placed in a cardboard tray. The exhibition catalogue records the type of clay, the colour of the glaze and the date on which the piece came out of the kiln.

In the main classroom, a tutor demonstrates how the shape of a handle changes the balance of a cup. Students compare several examples by drawing their outlines on squared paper. Some prefer a wide loop, while others choose a compact shape that follows the curve of the vessel. The discussion focuses on proportion, texture and the practical details of making a comfortable object.

The building used to be a small railway storehouse. Its windows face a courtyard where climbing plants cover an old brick wall. The renovation team retained the original beams and used pale tiles to reflect light into the work areas. A display near the door shows drawings of the building before and after the renovation, together with samples of the materials used.

Before closing, staff check the list of exhibition labels and adjust the spacing between the shelves. A volunteer tests the lights above the display cabinets. Another person folds information leaflets and sorts them by language. The opening event will include a short tour of the studio and a demonstration of how a lump of clay becomes a finished bowl.
zh:
社区果园位于铁路和公共步道之间的一条狭长地带。志愿者把工作笔记放在工具棚旁，方便每个小组了解上周末已经完成的事项。笔记记录浇水、修枝和更换木支架的情况。第一页的地图标明每排苹果树和梨树的品种。

春季开放日里，访客比较不同果树的花朵。讲解员介绍园丁如何观察最早出现的花芽，记录花瓣舒展的日期。孩子们画下树枝的轮廓，再把画作整理成册送到附近学校。几位老住户带来旧照片，展示果园建立之前这片土地的样子。

入口旁每月举行一次小集市。有的摊位出售手工编织的篮子，有的展示陶瓷杯盘。组织者测量场地，在桌子之间留出宽敞的通道。一位乐手在远处的大门旁弹奏木吉他，访客可以坐在长椅上，看列车从围栏外经过。

筹备会上，团队讨论公告栏的布局和新雨量计的位置。记录员为夏季各项活动制作简单的时间表，每件事都安排具体志愿者和大致完成日期。最后一个议题是一组旧地图，它们将在秋季采收活动中展出。

陶艺工作室正在筹备日常器皿展览。墙边的架子上摆着学生上学期制作的碗、杯子和小水壶。每件作品先放在尺子旁拍照，再装进纸板托盘。展览目录记录陶土种类、釉面颜色，以及作品出窑的日期。

主教室里，老师演示杯柄形状怎样影响杯子的平衡。学生把几个样品的轮廓画在方格纸上进行比较。有人喜欢宽大的环形把手，也有人选择贴近杯身曲线的小巧造型。讨论主要围绕比例、质感，以及怎样做出拿起来舒服的器物。

这栋建筑过去是一间铁路仓库。窗外的庭院里，攀缘植物覆盖着一面旧砖墙。改造团队保留了原来的横梁，用浅色瓷砖把光线反射到工作区域。门口的展板展示改造前后的图纸，还陈列了一些施工材料样本。

关门之前，工作人员核对展品标签，调整架子之间的距离。志愿者检查展柜上方的灯光，另一位成员折好介绍单页，按语言分类摆放。开幕活动包括简短参观和制作演示，让大家了解一团陶泥如何变成完整的碗。
